summary: Opposition politicians and government critics say arrests, prosecutions and restrictions on public activity are making it harder to challenge those in power. Is a broader pattern emerging?

title: Can Rassvet, 'Russia's Starlink' change the course of the war in Ukraine?
summary: SpaceX's US Starlink satellite system has played a key role in countering the Russian military in Ukraine, but now a Russian counterpart is under development. What could this mean for Ukraine in future?

title: Crew member dies after diesel tanker sinks off Ibiza coast
summary: Authorities rescued 17 crew members but one later died in hospital after a diesel tanker sank off the Spanish island of Ibiza. A contingency plan against possible pollution damage is now in place.

title: EU-Indonesia trade deal opens new markets, but challenges remain
summary: The agreement offers new export and investment opportunities for Jakarta and Brussels. But can Indonesia turn Europe's growing interest in its markets and critical minerals into sustainable gains at home?

title: EU leaders seek agreement on long-term budget and Ukraine at summit
summary: EU leaders have gathered to discuss the bloc's budget for 2028 to 2034. Amid competing demands, Hungary's Magyar has said he sees "zero chance" of a quick deal. Italy's Meloni said it's "light-years" away. DW has more.

title: Extreme weather threatens Thanksgiving festivities in US
summary: A major storm is forecast to move up the US East Coast and is likely to cause travel delays. Weather warnings were enough to postpone Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade for the first time in its 100 years.

title: FedEx plane overshoots runway at Miami airport on Thanksgiving eve
summary: A FedEx plane from Memphis ran past the end of a runway at Miami airport, shutting most runways and causing delays of several hours on the eve of the US holiday.

title: FIFA says a cyberattack against it targeted a 'limited set of personal and business information'
summary: World football's governing body says the cyberattack targeted personal and business information. They struck at a sensitive time for the under-fire organization and its president, Gianni Infantino.

title: Freigang banned — Germany star to miss 2027 World Cup
summary: Germany forward Laura Freigang has been suspended until October 2027 after missing three doping tests, ruling her out of next year's Women's World Cup in Brazil. Freigang has denied any intention to evade controls.

title: Germany: 2 arrested, suspected of plotting synagogue attack
summary: Federal prosecutors say they have ordered the arrest of two members of a pro-Iranian group on suspicion of planning an attack on a synagogue. They were detained in the cities of Heidelberg and Cologne.

title: Germany: IG Metall union says deal reached with employers
summary: IG Metall, representing millions of workers in Germany's metal and electrical industry, is the country's largest trade union. The deal came after more than 24 hours of talks with employers.

title: Germany news: Cologne court awards record damages in Catholic sex abuse case
summary: A court has awarded the highest damages ever in Germany to a victim of sexual abuse linked with the Catholic Church. An alleged spy and suspected terrorists are also making headlines in Germany on Thursday. DW has more.

title: Germany news: Final budget debate continues in Bundestag
summary: Spending for federal police and domestic intelligence are high on the agenda for parliamentary debate this Thursday. An alleged spy and suspected terrorists are also making headlines in Germany on Thursday. DW has more.

title: Health issues delay trial of Berlin woman accused of spying for Russia
summary: Prosecutors say the defendant used her political and military contacts to provide information on German defense and aid deliveries to Ukraine. Her arrest in January sparked a diplomatic row between Germany and Russia.

title: How Chinese companies circumvent chips sanctions in Southeast Asia
summary: High-tech AI chips are hard to get in China because of US restrictions. To get around this, Chinese companies often use offshore computing capacity, particularly in Southeast Asia. The US is also trying to stop it.

title: India news: Resolve tariff concerns in trade talks — India tells US
summary: India has denied US claims that New Delhi's policies promote excess manufacturing capacity. Further headlines from India include Constitution Day celebrations. DW has more.

title: Iranian drone attack kills 2 Italians in Kuwait
summary: The Italians were employed as technicians for the Italian branch of German arms manufacturer Rheinmetall. One Kuwaiti and one Pakistani national were also injured in the attack.

title: Is authoritarian Vietnam ready to phase out the death penalty?
summary: Vietnam has voted to abolish the death penalty for six more crimes, continuing a decades-long trend of restricting capital punishment.

title: Joshua Kimmich critcizes Bayern bosses over Musiala health comments
summary: Joshua Kimmich has slammed Bayern Munich's leadership over comments about Jamal Musiala's health issues. The bosses have questioned whether the player can return to previous form – and is still worth his high salary.

title: Kim Jong Un tours nuclear material sites, urges wider use of tactical nuclear weapons
summary: North Korea's Kim Jong Un visited sites that produce nuclear material and told his military to focus on tactical weapons, saying his country's nuclear status is irreversible.

title: Protests in Iraqi Kurdistan at plans for government in Baghdad to take over oil, border crossings
summary: Thousands have gathered in the capital of northern Iraq's semiautonomous Kurdish region, waving flags and voicing opposition to plans for the federal government to take control of oil operations and border crossings.

title: Russia-Ukraine war extends to the Baltic and the Mediterranean
summary: By attacking Russian vessels around the world, Kyiv is trying to up the pressure on Moscow and also sending out signals to its Western allies. What is the impact on global maritime trade?

title: US court blocks regulator's early review of ABC's broadcast licenses
summary: The FCC chairman had ordered an early review of ABC's licenses a day after President Donald Trump called for the broadcaster to fire Jimmy Kimmel earlier this year. The licenses were not set to expire until 2028.

title: What is the US permitting bill and would it actually help the climate?
summary: Sweeping US legislation to speed up energy projects has found rare bipartisan support. Supporters say it would unlock clean energy and lower energy bills, but critics say it's a gift to fossil fuels.
